text:
Morgan Rielly is 22 games into his 14th season in Toronto and still looking for his first goal. He has 12 assists, but he's also been part of a rough stretch for the Maple Leafs, who won three of his last ten games. He left the Nov. 7 game in Montreal after under six minutes, missed time, and returned against Chicago on Nov. 17.

Now there's trade talk. The Leafs Nation relayed a report from Pierre LeBrun: "Maple Leafs, Sharks discussed Morgan Rielly trade in the offseason." For a player who has spent all 973 of his NHL games with the team that drafted him fifth overall in 2012, that's a notable line to read in November.

Our numbers are mixed. His points pace (1.71 per 60) is actually above our talent range, carried by assists. The goals are a fluke in the other direction: zero on 1.66 expected. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 99th percentile for chances from in front of the net last season. The worry is defense: Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting more chances with him on the ice (bottom 5% of defensemen), and Toronto is outchanced in his minutes this season too.
headline: Rielly: no goals, and trade talk
